title: AAA 3 - How to Start Freelancing and more...
summary: Q&A episode with no code. Covers a staged route into freelancing, the instructor's daily work routine, native versus cross-platform mobile development, and a few productivity tools.

concepts.heading: Starting as a freelancer
points: Keep the day job at first; grow into freelancing gradually to limit risk.
Stage 1: set aside roughly 15 hours a week for a personal project that is genuinely useful to at least one person (not a hello-world or API experiment), deploy it, and treat it as portfolio material.

Stage 2: add roughly another 12-15 hours a week on small paid gigs from marketplaces such as Fiverr, Upwork or oDesk. Aim for experience, testimonials and references rather than income; keep early jobs under about a week.
Good starter work is what bigger agencies skip: bug fixes, updates, maintenance, small improvements.
Clear, regular communication with clients is the habit most likely to make or break a freelance career; repeat clients and word of mouth follow.

concepts.heading: Daily schedule ideas
points: Spend a protected block (about 1.5 hours) at your personal best time of day learning something new.
Put high-concentration creative work next, lighter tasks (editing, client meetings) later in the day.
Check email in one fixed slot rather than reacting to notifications; switching notifications off is the simple protection.
Walking meetings and matching tasks to your energy level are suggested for productivity.

concepts.heading: Native vs cross-platform apps
points: Native pros: best performance, strongest for animation and graphics, full access to platform APIs (push notifications, HealthKit), more community help.
Native cons: a separate Android build means a near-total rewrite, so more cost, time and developers.

Cross-platform tools (PhoneGap, Cordova, React Native) let web developers reuse JavaScript skills; React Native sits in the middle but sometimes needs custom native code for standard features, and its licence terms were seen as a drawback.
Conclusion: no blanket rule; judge each project's needs.

concepts.heading: Tools mentioned
points: Product Hunt for discovering products; Duet (turn an iPad/iPhone into a second screen); Alfred (faster Mac launcher than Spotlight); Momentum (new-tab dashboard with to-do and focus task); CheatSheet (hold Cmd to list an app's shortcuts).

pitfalls: Quitting a job to freelance before building a portfolio and client base is the main risk called out.
Taking large, ambitious first gigs instead of small ones.
